The counters appeared once again in Urza's Destiny on Festering Wound which had a similar effect. In this case it was an enchantment for a creature which created a counter on each upkeep. It would then deal damage to the creature's controller each upkeep based on the number of infection counters on it.
Infection counter.use: Deals Damage to opponent Player on Upkeep

Influence counter.intro: Influence counters are a type of counter introduced in The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-Earth.
Influence counter.description: Influence counters first appeared on Palantír of Orthanc to track the number of cards milled. They represent the growing influence of Sauron on those who use the Palantír.
Influence counter.use: Upkeep tracking for corruption by Sauron

Ingenuity counter.intro: Ingenuity counters are a type of counter introduced in Dominaria United. They act as a resource for an ability to cast artifacts without paying their mana cost.
Ingenuity counter.description: Ingenuity counters first appeared on Jhoira, Ageless Innovator in Dominaria United. Jhoira has an activated ability to add two Ingenuity counters to itself which then allows the free casting of an artifact from the player's hand with a mana value less than or equal to the number of cards on it. They represent the artificer's ability for innovating and creating the artifacts. Lady Octopus, Inspired Inventor also uses these counters which allows her to free cast artifacts. Lady Octopus gains these counters however by drawing cards.
Ingenuity counter.use: Counter for the ability to cast artifacts without their mana cost.

Intel counter.intro: Intel counters are a type of counter introduced in Transformers. They act as a marker on exiled cards that may return to the player's hand in the future.
Intel counter.description: Intel counters first appeared on Flamewar, Brash Veteran//Flamewar, Streetwise Operative in Transformers. The card in question uses the More Than Meets the Eye mechanic to transform into the other. The Streetwise Operative form is a vehicle that is also a creature due to Living Metal. When it attacks, it transforms and exiles cards with the counter on them from the top of the player’s library equal to the number of damage it deals when attacking. The Brash Veteran form has an ability that lets the player discard their hand and return all the exiled cards with the counter on them to the player's hand. The type marks the cards as future Intel that the player may use.
Intel counter.use: Marker on exile for potential return to hand

Intervention counter.intro: Intervention counter are a type of counter introduced in Legends. They act as a tracker for an alternate-draw condition making it so neither player wins or loses.
Intervention counter.description: Intervention counters first appeared on Divine Intervention in Legends and later re-printed in Masters Edition III. They were originally unnamed counters but were later errated into Intervention counters. The enchantment enters play with 2 of these counters on it with one being removed on each upkeep. Once all are removed, the game ends as a draw making it so neither player wins or loses. The alternate draw condition only triggers when the final counter is removed by the controller.

Invitation counter.intro: Invitation counters are a type of counter introduced in Innistrad: Crimson Vow. It acts as a counter for the transform mechanic of double-faced cards.
Invitation counter.description: Invitation counters first appeared on Wedding Announcement in Innistrad: Crimson Vow. One of the counters is added to the enchantment at the beginning of the player's end step. After 3 or more counters build up on it, then it transforms into Wedding Festivity. The counters represent the invitations being sent out before the wedding starts.

Isolation counter.intro: Isolation counters are a type of counter introduced in Battle for Zendikar. They act as a count for the temporary exile of cards.
Isolation counter.description: Isolation counters first appeared on Quarantine Field in Battle for Zendikar. It is an enchantment that enters the battlefield with Isolation counters equal to the additional mana spent to cast it. It will then exile nonland permanents for each isolation counter on it until the enchantment leaves the battlefield at which point they are returned to play. Its name represents its effect in that the permanents are being isolated while it is in play.

Javelin counter.intro: Javelin counters are a type of counter introduced in Fallen Empires. They act as a resource for damaging a creature or player.
Javelin counter.description: Javelin counters first appeared on Icatian Javelineers in Fallen Empires and later re-printed in various sets. It is a creature that enters the battlefield with a single Javelin counter on it which it can then use to deal 1 damage to a creature or player via an activated ability. This represents the creature throwing its javelin to cause damage.
Javelin counter.use: Deals 1 damage to a creature or player

Judgment counter.intro: Judgment counters are a type of counter introduced in Innistrad: Crimson Vow.
Judgment counter.description: Judgment counters first appeared on the Double-faced card Faithbound Judge and Sinner's Judgment in Innistrad: Crimson Vow. On both forms of the card, the counters act as an upkeep tracker where they build up to 3 for different effects. By default the creature has Defender but when it gets to 3 or more counters it can attack as though it does not. For the enchantment, it is an aura curse that acts as an alternate loss condition in which the player loses the game once it reaches 3 or more counters.

Keyword counter.intro: A Keyword counter is a counter that gives a keyword ability to a permanent they're on. The game mechanic was featured in Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths.
Keyword counter.description:
A permanent with a keyword counter on it gains that keyword. Use the counter's timestamp to determine how this interacts with continuous effects. The timestamp of a counter is the most recent time that any counter was put onto the permanent.

For this group of counters, having more than one of the same counter provides no additional benefit. Note that if these counters end up on a noncreature permanent, it won't necessarily apply immediately, but it will if the permanent becomes a creature. The exceptions here are exalted, hexproof, and indestructible, which work even if they end up on a noncreature permanent. Deathtouch and lifelink counters could also matter if the noncreature permanent can deal damage.

During its introduction in Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths, several spells rewarded creatures with particular keywords (keyword "lords"), as well as multiple creatures and spells that granted the choice of several keywords.

Ki counter.intro: Ki counters (KEE) are placed on permanents, whenever you cast a spirit or arcane spell. Ki counters belong to the unofficially named spiritcraft ability word used during the Kamigawa block. According to Chinese and Japanese lore, Ki is the vital force that forms part of any living thing.
Ki counter.description: There is a common cycle (the Bakus), an uncommon cycle (the flip card legends), and one rare (Baku Altar) that uses this counter. The Bakus use them with a payment of and remove any number for a scaling effect. The uncommon cycle is all 1CC 2/2 creatures that set their flip condition at having two ki counters at the end of the turn, flip into a Legendary Spirit who has an ability that removes one ki counter - this notably prevents them from "recharging" ki counters.

Kick counter.intro: Kick counters are a type of counter introduced in the Secret Lair Drop Series: February Superdrop 2022. They are created via multikicker and allow the player to cast copies of exiled instants on the creature's attack.
Kick counter.description:
Kick counters first appeared on Chun-Li, Countless Kicks in the Street Fighter drop of the Secret Lair Drop Series: February Superdrop 2022. It has the multikicker mechanic on it which also allows for the creature to exile instants from the graveyard with a Kick counter on them for how many times she was kicked. Then, via her Lightning Kick Flavor word ability, Chun-Li can copy and cast any of the exiled cards with a counter each time she attacks. They are used thematically to represent the power and speed of Chun-Li's kicks.

When Chun-Li's Universes Within counterpart was printed in Phyrexia: All Will Be One, kick counters were not renamed.
Kick counter.use: Cast copies of exiled instants on the creature's attack

Knickknack counter.intro: Knickknack counters are a type of counter introduced in Unfinity. They act as an alternate +1/+1 counter with an additional aspect that they must be each represented by a unique item that fits on the card.
Knickknack counter.description: Knickknack counters first appeared on the acorn card Tchotchke Elemental in Unfinity. It is a creature that gains a Knickknack counter whenever a counter or sticker is placed on a card or a token is created. The card specifies that the player uses a unique item that completely fits on Tchotchke Elemental for each knickknack counter. This represents the elemental collecting knickknacks.

Knowledge counter.intro: Knowledge counters are a type of counter introduced in the Throne of Eldraine. They act as an upkeep tracker for the player drawing more cards each turn.
Knowledge counter.description: Knowledge counters first appeared on The Magic Mirror in Throne of Eldraine. It is a Legendary Artifact which gains a Knowledge counter each upkeep. Alongside that, for each counter on it, the player may draw a card. The artifact also makes it so the player has no maximum hand size to counteract many cards being drawn each turn. The counters thematically represent the player gaining knowledge via the Magic Mirror.
Knowledge counter.use: Upkeep tracker; draw card for each counter

Landmark counter.intro: Landmark counters are a type of counter introduced in Ixalan. They act as a tracker for the transform mechanic and the creation of Treasure tokens.
Landmark counter.description: Landmark counters first appeared on Treasure Map in Ixalan. It can Scry while adding a Landmark counter after each use of it. Once 3 counters are on the artifact, it then transforms and creates 3 Treasure tokens. The tokens can then either be sacrificed for colorless mana or card draw. The naming of the counters represents the finding of Landmarks with a treasure in them.
Landmark counter.use: Tracker for transform and Treasure token creation

Level counter.intro: Level counters are exclusively used by the Level up mechanic. They are used to track levels on Leveler cards.

Loot counter.intro: Loot counters are a type of counter first introduced in Outlaws of Thunder Junction.
Loot counter.description: Loot counters were introduced in Outlaws of Thunder Junction on Bandit's Haul. They are used as a thematic representation of the proceeds of crime. Bandit's Haul is an artifact that gets loot counters added to it as the players commit crimes, representing the increasing riches gained by thieving. The player is then able to use an activated ability for 2 colorless mana to remove 2 loot counters and draw a card.
Loot counter.use: Tracking how many crimes a player has committed; Drawing a card

Lore counter.intro: Lore counters are a type of counter introduced in Magic 2012 but later became more commonly related to Sagas allowing for tracking what chapter of the saga is active.
Lore counter.description:
Lore counters first appeared in Magic 2012 with Mind Unbound where they acted as an upkeep tracker for how many cards the enchantment would let the player draw each turn. Two other uses of lore counters were with Scroll of the Masters in Fate Reforged and Myth Realized in Dragons of Tarkir. Both of these gains a Lore counter every time a noncreature spell is cast by the player and then can add power and toughness onto the board equal to the lore counters: Scroll of the Masters gives it to other creatures, while Myth Realized does so by animating into a creature. The insinuation of Myth Realized is that it is a manifestation of the lost Scroll of the Masters. Myth Realized can also add lore counters for mana. These original three usages were unrelated to the Sagas these counters later became more known for.

With the introduction of Sagas in Dominaria, Lore counters became an integral part of that enchantment type as they acted as the tracker for which chapter of the Saga was activated, adding one each pre-combat main phase. Subsequent sets with Sagas continued to use Lore counters on them.

In later sets, some cards had effects that put extra Lore counters on sagas. Keldon Warcaller in Dominaria would add them on Sagas whenever it attacked. Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty later introduced Satsuki, the Living Lore which had an activated ability to put Lore counters on sagas while Storyweave was a modal instant that in which one of the effects was adding two Lore counters to a saga.

Loyalty counter.intro: Loyalty counters are counters that are used to track the loyalty of planeswalkers. With 317 planeswalker cards and 23 more cards that interact with loyalty counters, they are the second most common counter type in Magic, behind +1/+1 counters at 2,964 cards.
Loyalty counter.description:
Loyalty counters are almost exclusively connected to planeswalker cards and are usually added or removed to activate loyalty abilities. Other abilities can cause them to gain or lose loyalty as well. Planeswalkers enter play with the number of loyalty counters printed on their card due to an intrinsic ability, lose loyalty counters corresponding to damage dealt to them, and go to the graveyard when they have no loyalty counters on them as a state-based action.

Gatewatch Beacon from Commander Masters is the first non-planeswalker card to enter the battlefield with loyalty counters on it.

Luck counter.intro: Luck counters are a type of counter introduced in Legends. They usually are created by some form of randomness like Flipping a coin or Dice rolling and lead to an alternate win condition or grant a permanent more beneficial ability.
Luck counter.description:
Luck counters first appeared on Chance Encounter in Odyssey. It is an enchantment that would add a luck counter any time the player wins a coin flip. If the number of Luck counters builds up to 10 or more, then the player wins the game.

The counters appeared once again on Gemstone Caverns in Time Spiral with a different usage. This time the counter was used with land in that if the land appeared in the player's opening hand they could begin the game with it on the battlefield with a luck counter on it in exchange for exiling a different card from the player's hand. The land has an ability that by default just gives colorless mana but when a luck counter is on it, it gives mana of any color.
Luck counter.use: alternate win conditions or more beneficial ability

Magnet counter.intro: Magnet counters are a type of counter introduced in Tempest. They give an effect to creatures that force them to attack or block when others with the counter do so.
Magnet counter.description: Magnet counters first appeared on Magnetic Web in Tempest. It had an activated ability to place Magnet counters on creatures. Whenever a creature with a Magnet counter on it attacks, all other creatures with them on it are forced to attack as well. Similarly, whenever a creature with a Magnet counter on it blocks another creature, all other creatures with them are forced to block as well. These effects represent a magnetic pull between the creatures with the counters.
Magnet counter.use: Forces creatures to attack and block together

Manabond counter.intro: Several mechanics are unique to playtest cards from Mystery Booster, Mystery Booster 2, and Unknown Events. This list includes all such mechanics alphabetically from L–Q. Many of them appear on only one card.

Manifestation counter.intro: Manifestation counters are a type of counter introduced in Born of the Gods. They are spawned via the Inspired mechanic and turn Permanents into Enchantments in addition to their other types.
Manifestation counter.description: Manifestation counters first appeared on Arbiter of the Ideal in Born of the Gods. They are created via the Inspired mechanic in that whenever the creature is untapped, the top card of the library is revealed and if it’s an artifact, creature, or land then it can be put onto the battlefield with one of the counters on it. It makes that artifact, creature, or lands an enchantment in addition to its other types. The name of the counter refers to the permanent being manifested onto the battlefield as an enchantment.
Manifestation counter.use: Permanent becomes Enchantment in addition to other types

Mannequin counter.intro: Mannequin counters are a type of counter introduced in Lorwyn. They represent a creature being a mannequin rather than the actual creature.
Mannequin counter.description: Mannequin counters first appeared on Makeshift Mannequin in Lorwyn. It is an Instant which returns a creature from the graveyard with one of the counters on it. With the counter on it, it also gains the effect of forcing its sacrifice if it becomes the target of a spell or ability. This represents the creature being turned into a mannequin rather than returning from the graveyard.
Mannequin counter.use: Creature sacrificed when targeted by spell or ability

Matrix counter.intro: Matrix counters are a type of counter introduced in Legends. They allow for a player to regenerate a creature.
Matrix counter.description: Matrix counters first appeared on Life Matrix in Legends as an unnamed counter type which was later given errata to be Matrix counters. It was an artifact which had an activated ability to add Matrix counters to creatures. The counter could then be removed during upkeep to regenerate the creature.

Memory counter.intro: Memory counters are a type of counter introduced in Assassin's Creed.
Memory counter.description: Memory counters first appeared in Assassin's Creed. Creatures exiled with memory counters on them can have a token copy created of them when conditions are met. This emulates the ability to relive the memories of ancestors, which features prominently in the Assassin's Creed games.
Memory counter.use: Marker on exiled creature. Tapped attacking token copy created during combat and exiled after.

Midway counter.intro: Midway counter are a type of counter introduced in Unfinity. They are counters that are placed on attractions that allow copies of certain spells when they are visited.
Midway counter.description: Midway counters first appeared on Myra the Magnificent in Unfinity. It is a creature with an activated ability that lets it put a Midway counter on an attraction alongside exiling an instant or sorcery. Whenever the player visits that attraction, they can copy the exiled card and cast the copy without paying its mana cost.
Midway counter.use: Cast copies of exiled instants and sorceries when attraction is visited

Mine counter.intro: Mine counters are a type of counter introduced in Odyssey. They are placed on lands, which were destroyed if the land becomes tapped.
Mine counter.description: Mine counters first appeared on Mine Layer in Tempest. It was a creature that had an activated ability to place Mine counters on lands. Whenever a land with one of the counters became tapped it would be destroyed. The mine counters only remained for as long as Mine Layer was on the battlefield. This represented landmines being placed on the lands and blowing up the land upon its use.
Mine counter.use: Destroys land when it becomes tapped

Mining counter.intro: Mining counters are a type of counter introduced in Weatherlight. They acted as a limited amount of mana on lands.
Mining counter.description: Mining counters first appeared on Gemstone Mine in Weatherlight. It was a colorless land that entered the battlefield with 3 mining counters on it. These could then be used each turn to add mana of any color. After all the mining counters were removed the Gemstone Mine was sacrificed. They represent the gems of the Mine being mined until its exhausted of resources.
Mining counter.use: Limited amount of mana on a land

Mire counter.intro: Mire counters are a type of counter used by Cyclopean Tomb, first printed in Alpha. They turn lands into Swamps.
Mire counter.description: The original Alpha printing of Cyclopean Tomb referred to the counters as "tokens", before being given errata and being re-printed as Mire counters. Cyclopean Tomb is an artifact with an activated ability to place the counter on a non-Swamp land. The land then becomes a Swamp. After the artifact leaves the battlefield, on each subsequent upkeep all of the counters are removed from 1 land, which removes the effect from that land.

Music counter.intro: Music counters are a type of counter introduced in Ice Age. They force a player to pay mana to prevent a creature from being destroyed.
Music counter.description: Music counters first appeared on Musician in Ice Age and later re-printed digitally in Masters Edition II. It has an activated ability to place Music counters on creatures. For each music counter on a creature, the player must pay one mana each turn, or else it'll be destroyed. The counters and ability remain even after the Musician leaves the battlefield.
Music counter.use: Requires mana payment to prevent the creature from being destroyed

Muster counter.intro: Muster counters are a type of counter introduced in Gatecrash. They act as an upkeep tracker for creating soldier tokens.
Muster counter.description: Muster counters first appeared on Assemble the Legion in Gatecrash. It is an enchantment that gains a Muster counter each upkeep. Then, a 1/1 red and white Soldier token is created for each Muster counter on it. This represents the soldiers being assembled for battle.
Muster counter.use: Upkeep tracker for creating Soldier tokens

Necrodermis counter.intro: Necrodermis counters are a type of counter introduced in the Warhammer 40,000 Commander Decks. They revive creatures from the graveyard as artifact creatures.
Necrodermis counter.description: Necrodermis counters first appeared on The War in Heaven in the Warhammer 40,000 Commander Decks. It is a Saga whose third Lore counter ability lets the player return a creature from the graveyard to the battlefield with a total mana value of 8 or less. They return to the battlefield as artifact creature in addition to their other types. This represents the creature bonding with the Necrodermis.
Necrodermis counter.use: Creature returns from the graveyard to the battlefield as an artifact creature

Nest counter.intro: Nest counters are a type of counter introduced in Duskmourn: House of Horror.
Nest counter.description: Nest counters first appeared in Duskmourn: House of Horror on Twitching Doll. It is an Spider Toy that appears as a doll with numerous spiders living within it. The counters are made to represent the growing ranks of spiders within the doll itself. It has an activated ability that adds mana and agains one of the counters. It has an additional activated ability to sacrifice itself to become a 2/2 green spider with reach for each counter on the doll.
Nest counter.use: Marker for number of spider tokens to create

Net counter.intro: Net counters are a type of counter introduced in Fallen Empires. They are used for effects that freeze a permanent.
Net counter.description:
Net counters first appeared on Merseine in Fallen Empires. It is an aura enchantment that enters the battlefield with 3 net counters on it. The enchanted creature cannot be untapped for as long as it has Net counters on it. The player can pay the creature's mana cost to remove one of the counters. This represents the creature being encased in a net unless it expends energy to escape.

Their next appearance was on the artifact Braided Net in The Lost Caverns of Ixalan. Rather than being removed to free a creature, they are removed to tap a nonland permanent and disable its abilities for the turn.

Night counter.intro: Night counters are a type of counter introduced in Kaldheim. They act as an upkeep tracker for a triggered token creation effect.
Night counter.description: Night counters first appeared on Replicating Ring in Kaldheim. It is a snow artifact that can add one mana of any color and one of the counters is added on the player's upkeep each turn. Once it reaches eight or more counters, they are all removed and eight Snow Artifact tokens known as Replicated Ring are created with the ability to create one mana of any color.

Oil counter.intro: Oil counters are a counter type in Magic. They were introduced in Phyrexia: All Will Be One.
Oil counter.description:
Oil counters are a type of counters without inherent rules meaning, but are flavorly tied to the glistening oil.

Permanents that interact with oil counters do so in different ways—some spend them to activate abilities, others require a certain amount or more of them to activate abilities, and some scale their effects based on the number of oil counters present on themselves or other permanents.

Oil counters were designed to synergize with proliferate, ensuring that having more is always beneficial. For example, if a creature has a limited lifespan based on oil counters it has, it would start with a set amount of oil counters and counts down rather than counting up. This design allows proliferate to extend its lifespan rather than hastening its removal.

Omen counter.intro: Omen counters are a type of counter introduced in Prophecy. They act as markers leading up to either an alternate-win condition or the transform mechanic to activate after a certain number of them build up or are removed. This represents the 'Omen' in their name as they lead up to an event happening.
Omen counter.description:
Omen counters first appeared on Celestial Convergence in Prophecy. It acts as a tracker for an alternate-win condition whereas the enchantment enters play with 7 Omen counters on it with 1 removed each Upkeep. When no more counters remain, then the player with the highest life wins the game or it ends in a draw of the players have equal life.

The counters appeared once again in Innistrad: Crimson Vow on Foreboding Statue and Soulcipher Board. In both of these cases, they acted as a marker for the transform mechanic. For Foreboding Statue, it had an ability that added an omen counter to it when activated. It would then transform into Forsaken Thresher after having 3 or more of the counters on it. For Soulcipher Board, it enters play with 3 omen counters on it and one is removed for each card that enters the graveyard. It then transforms into Cipherbound Spirit when all the counters are removed.
Omen counter.use: Marker for alternate-win condition and transform mechanic

Ore counter.intro: Ore counters are a type of counter introduced in Homelands. They mark a land for eventual destruction damaging the player upon their eventual removal.
Ore counter.description: Ore counters first appeared on Orcish Mine in Homelands. The enchantment is an aura that enchants a land and starts with 3 Ore counters on it. One gets removed each time the land is tapped and at the player's upkeep. Once all 3 are removed the land gets destroyed and the player receives 2 damage. This represents the land being exhausted of resources until it collapses damaging the player using it.
Ore counter.use: Land destruction and damage to a player

Page counter.intro: Page counters are a type of counter introduced in Urza's Saga. They often are used for tracking the upkeep or ability usage of some sort of book artifact.
Page counter.description:
Page counters first appeared in the Urza block on two cards. First Barrin's Codex in Urza's Saga made use of them as an upkeep tracker. It is an artifact with an activated ability to sacrifice itself to allow the player to draw cards equal to the number of Page counters on it. Private Research in Urza's Destiny had a similar usage where they acted as an upkeep tracker once again allowing for cards to be drawn equal to the number of counters whenever an enchanted creature died.

Throne of Eldraine saw the counter's return on Tome of Legend, a Commander specific card. It would enter the battlefield with one Page counter and gain more every time a Commander enters the battlefield or attacks. They could then be exchanged for a card draw via an activated ability. Mazemind Tome from Core Set 2021 had Page counters act as a tracker for how many times the artifact's abilities with it being exiled once it hit 4 or more counters also giving the player 4 life.

The first non-artifact usage appeared on Tasha, the Witch Queen in Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate. In this case, the Planeswalker could exile cards in the opponent's graveyards and use another to cast any card in exile with a page counter without paying their mana cost.

The counters appeared again in Unfinity on Autograph Book which is an Acorn artifact that enters the battlefield with a page counter for each person that has signed the book. They then act as a resource for an ability that lets the player draw a card.

The various types of Page counters do not currently interact with each other.

Pain counter.intro: Pain counters are a type of counter introduced in Tempest. They are used to deal damage to a creature but can also deal damage to the player using them as well.
Pain counter.description: Pain counters first appeared on Torture Chamber in Tempest. It is an artifact that gains a Pain counter each upkeep. It then has an activated ability to remove all pain counters and deals damage to the target creature equal to the counters removed. If the counters are not removed during a turn and remain on it during the end step, the player takes damage equal to the number of counters.

Palliation counter.intro: Palliation counters are a type of counter introduced in Dissension, used only on the card Palliation Accord.
Palliation counter.description:
Palliation counters first appeared on Palliation Accord in Dissension where they were originally known as shield counters before being renamed to "palliation counters" when shield counters were added as a mechanic in Streets of New Capenna.

Palliation Accord is an enchantment that gets a palliation counter placed on it whenever an opponent's permanent becomes tapped. The player may then remove one of the palliation counters to prevent 1 damage from being dealt to the player during the turn it was removed.
Palliation counter.use: Prevent 1 damage dealt to the player during the turn it is removed

Paralyzation counter.intro: Paralyzation counters are a type of counter introduced in Ice Age. They freeze a creature for as long as they are on one.
Paralyzation counter.description: Paralyzation counters first appeared on Dread Wight in Ice Age. It was a creature that would put a Paralyzation counter on any creature that blocked or was blocked by it. These counters caused the creatures to be tapped and freezes them. Each of the creatures also gains an ability to pay to remove the counter from it. The freezing represents the creature being paralyzed by the Wight.

Pause counter.intro: Pause counters are a type of counter introduced in Unfinity. They are an acorn effect that lets the player pause an effect that normally would only last for the turn and extend it longer.
Pause counter.description: Pause counters first appeared on the acorn Grand Marshal Macie in Unfinity. The play can choose to not untap the creature in exchange for it getting a Pause counter and the player taking 1 life per counter. All the counters are removed if it is ever untapped. It has an activated ability that lets the player choose an “until end of turn” or “this turn” effect which will remain active until the creature is untapped. This act as if the effect is being Paused by the counters with an increasing cost to the player taking more life each turn.
Pause counter.use: “Until end of turn” or “this turn” effects do not end until the creature is untapped

Petal counter.intro: Petal counters are a type of counter introduced in Urza's Saga that built up and were sacrificed for mana.
Petal counter.description: Petal counters first appeared on Lotus Blossom in Urza's Saga. It was an artifact which got a Petal counter added on it each upkeep. It then had a special activated ability that could be activated as a mana source to sacrifice it to create mana of one color for however many Petal counters were on it. This represented the petals of the lotus being cultivated for mana.

Petrification counter.intro: Petrification counters are a type of counter introduced in Magic 2013. They represent a Gorgon's ability to turn a creature to stone.
Petrification counter.description: Petrification counters first appeared on Xathrid Gorgon in Magic 2013. It is a creature with the ability to put a petrification counter on a creature. The Gorgon's ability causes target creature to become a colorless artifact with Defender and which cannot use any of its abilities. These effects represent the creature being a stone statue of itself. The effect is not tied to the counter. If the counter is removed, the creature remains a colorless artifact with Defender and cannot use any of its abilities. If the counter is transferred to another creature, that creature does not become a colorless artifact with Defender and can still use its abilities.
Petrification counter.use: Creature becomes a colorless artifact with Defender which can't activate its abilities

Phyresis counter.intro: Phyresis counters are a type of counter introduced in Dominaria United. They are related to the Phyrexians.
Phyresis counter.description: Phyresis counters first appeared on the Weatherlight Compleated in Dominaria United. It is a vehicle that gains a Phyresis counter each time a creature dies under the player's control. Once it reaches 4 or more of the counters, it becomes a Phyrexian creature along with its other types. Up until it has 7 counters the player can scry 1 and once it hits 7 or more they can draw a card. They represent the ship becoming more corrupted by Glistening oil.
Phyresis counter.use: Various effects based on the number of counters

Phylactery counter.intro: Phylactery counters are a type of counter introduced in Magic 2011. They are used to represent a lich's soul being stored in an artifact.
Phylactery counter.description: Phylactery counters first appeared on Phylactery Lich in Magic 2011. It is a creature that adds a phylactery counter on an artifact when it enters the battlefield. The Lich is Indestructible but must then be sacrificed whenever the player doesn't control a permanent with a Phylactery counter on it. This represents the artifact being turned into a Phylactery for the Lich.

Pin counter.intro: Pin counters are a type of counter introduced in Legends. They act as upkeep trackers representing pins of a voodoo doll.
Pin counter.description: Pin counters first appeared on Voodoo Doll in Fallen Empires as unnamed counters before they were given errata to be Pin counters. It is an artifact that gets a Pin counter for each upkeep and has an activated ability that costs double the number of counters for its mana cost to deal damage equal to the number of the counters. If the artifact is not tapped at the player's end step then it is sacrificed along with dealing damage to the player equal to the number of counters. This represents the player putting pins into a Voodoo doll along with it being cursed forcing the player to continue using it or it turns on them.

Plague counter.intro: Plague counters are a type of counter introduced in Odyssey. They've behaved as both −1/−1 counters and as a type of upkeep tracking counter.
Plague counter.description:
Plague counters first appeared on Traveling Plague in Odyssey. It is an enchantment that when placed on a creature will create a plague counter on it with each upkeep. These counters will act as −1/−1 counters. They appeared once again on Withering Hex in Onslaught. The counters behaved the same way off of this enchantment but were instead created whenever a card was cycled.

Plague Boiler in Ravnica: City of Guilds saw their return as a resource. In this case, they acted differently in that they represented the regulation of the boiler. A plague counter was added to it at every upkeep and if more than three were on it then it would destroy all non-land permanents. It, however, had an ability that allowed a counter to either be added or removed as well as giving more control to the player for when it takes effect.

Plot counter.intro: Plot counters are a type of counter introduced in Conspiracy: Take the Crown. They are created by an ability that can be activated by any player in the game since Conspiracy is made for multiple players.
Plot counter.description: Plot counters first appeared on Deadly Designs in Conspiracy: Take the Crown and later re-printed in Masters 25. It is an enchantment with an ability that can be activated by any player which adds Plot counters to it. Then should it build up to 5 or more Plot counters, the enchantment is sacrificed in exchange for destroying 2 creatures. Its ability to allow multiple players to activate it represents a plot between players to destroy enemy creatures at a designated time.

Point counter.intro: Point counters are a type of counter introduced in Strixhaven: School of Mages. They act as a tracking mechanism for game related actions.
Point counter.description:
Cards that use point counters thematically represent the back-and-forth of a sports game where points are gained or lost.

Point counters first appeared on the Strixhaven Stadium in Strixhaven: School of Mages. It is an artifact with an activated ability to add 1 colorless mana and a point counter on the artifact. If a creature deals combat damage to the player then a point counter is removed and whenever a creature the player controls deals damage another point counter is added to it. If the artifact reaches 10 or more counters then the player who was dealt damage and caused the last counter to be added loses the game.

The Lost Caverns of Ixalan used point counters on Contested Game Ball; a similarly sport themed card. Rather than being used as an alternate lose condition, it is used to track who "wins" the prize of a Treasure token.

The 2024 Las Vegas Planechase Unknown featured the counters on Raider's Allegiance which was a plane card that got one of them during the second main phase for each other player that was dealt damage to. Then whenever it was planeswalked away from, the player with the most point counters got three treasure tokens and removed all the counters.

The 2025 Atlanta Unknown Event later interacted them on Brave Falconhawk which created Contested Game Ball tokens and gave +1/+1 counters for each point counter when it attacked.
Point counter.use: Tracking the "score" of a sport-themed minigame

Poison counter.intro: A poison counter is a counter that, unlike most other counters, is placed on players rather than objects. When a player has ten or more poison counters, that player loses the game. A player with at least one poison counter is considered poisoned. Interacting with poison counters is seen mostly in black and green.
Poison counter.use: A player with ten or more poison counters loses the game.

Polyp counter.intro: Polyp counters are a type of counter introduced in Homelands that acted as a resource for creating +0/+1 counters.
Polyp counter.description: Polyp counters first appeared on Coral Reef in Homelands. It is an enchantment that enters the battlefield with 4 polyp counters on it. Additional counters are added to it via the sacrifice of islands. These counters then served as the resource for an activated ability that tapped a creature while adding an +0/+1 counter to a creature.

Possession counter.intro: Possession counters are a type of counter introduced in Duskmourn: House of Horror. They represent the amount of influence or control an evil being has over its possessed host.
Possession counter.description: Possession counters first appeared on Unwilling Vessel. One of the counters is added whenever an enchantment is added or a room is fully unlocked. When the creature dies, a X/X blue Spirit creature token with flying with X being the number of counters. This represents the spirit possessing the unwilling vessel being released.
Possession counter.use: Tracking the size of the possessing spirit

Pressure counter.intro: Pressure counters are a type of counter introduced in Visions. They acted as an increasing resource for a sacrificial ability.
Pressure counter.description:
Pressure counters first appeared on Magma Mine in Visions. It was an artifact that could add Pressure counters to itself. It could also be sacrificed at any time dealing +1 damage for each counter on it. The counters represented the magma pressure building up until it exploded with the sacrifice ability.

They reappeared again in Magic 2013 with Hellion Crucible which was a land that also could add Pressure counters to itself. It only needed to build up 2 before it could be sacrificed to create a 4/4 red Hellion creature token with Haste. In this case, the counters represented the pressure building up until a Hellion is born.

Prey counter.intro: Prey counter are a type of counter introduced in Rivals of Ixalan. They act as a marker for a creature's potential death.
Prey counter.description: Prey counters first appeared on Tetzimoc, Primal Death in Rivals of Ixalan. The creature has an ability that could be used from a player's hand that would add a Prey counter to a creature. Then whenever it entered the battlefield, it would automatically destroy all of an opponent's creatures with the Prey counter on it regardless of how they ended up on the creature. This represented Tetzimoc being one of the apex predators due to it being one of the Elder Dinosaurs of Ixalan.
Prey counter.use: Marker for a creature's potential death.

Pupa counter.intro: Pupa counters are a type of counter introduced in Legends that would freeze a creature until they were removed, giving that creature a power-up.
Pupa counter.description: Pupa counters first appeared on Cocoon in Legends originally as Change counters before they were given errata to be Pupa counters. Cocoon is an Aura enchantment that taps the creature with 3 Pupa counters. The creature remains tapped while the counters are on it, with one removed for each upkeep. Then, after all are removed, the enchantment is sacrificed, and the creature gains a +1/+1 counter and flying. This represents the creature frozen in the cocoon for several turns until it emerges stronger.
Pupa counter.use: Freeze creature and power-up on removal

Quest counter.intro: Quest counters are used for multiple cycles of enchantments from Zendikar block and returned in Universes Beyond: Fallout, Avatar: The Last Airbender, and Modern Horizons 3. They mark the progress of the informally named "quest" enchantments.

Rad counter.intro: A rad counter is a counter that is placed on players rather than objects. A card that refers to life loss “from radiation” refers to life lost as a result of the triggered ability associated with rad counters. Rad counters were introduced as part of Universes Beyond: Fallout.
Rad counter.description:
Rad counters represent your current radiation levels, and the higher that is, the more serious the impact. Rad counters, unlike most other counters, have an inherent ability: At the beginning of the precombat main phase of a player with rad counters, that player mills cards equal to the number of rad counters they have. For each nonland card milled this way, that player loses 1 life and removes one rad counter from themselves. This process is referred to as "radiation". In the long term, each rad counter is a point of damage, but reflecting the phenomenon of radioactive half-lives, the decay is probabilistic rather than guaranteed. This ability is represented by the Radiation helper card.

Rad counters may strengthen cards but come with the risk of death. To avoid being overly parasitic, most cards that are strengthened by rad counters use a trigger based off milling nonland cards.

The mechanical execution of rad counters may be reused in future sets, but possibly not under the same name.
Rad counter.use: At the beginning of your precombat main phase, if you have any rad counters, mill that many cards. For each nonland card milled this way, you lose 1 life and a rad counter.

Rally counter.intro: Rally counter are a type of counter introduced in the Jeskai Striker commander deck for Tarkir: Dragonstorm.
Rally counter.description: Rally counters were introduced on Aligned Heart as a thematic way of representing the monks of the Jeskai Way coming together to defend their clan. The counters have no inherent connection with either the Monk tokens produced by Aligned Heart or the ability word of the same name.

Rejection counter.intro: Rejection counters are a type of counter introduced in March of the Machine: The Aftermath. They represent the removal and rejection of unwanted invaders and creatures
Rejection counter.description: Rejection counters first appeared on Tolarian Contempt in March of the Machine: The Aftermath. It enters and puts the counters on all creatures that opponents control. At the end step, one of those creatures (one for each opponent) gets tucked.

Reprieve counter.intro: Reprieve counters are a type of counter introduced in Jumpstart 2022. They can be used to return creatures to the battlefield on their death. This represents them getting a reprieve from death.
Reprieve counter.description: Reprieve counters first appeared on the Magnanimous Magistrate in Jumpstart 2022. Five reprieve counters are added to the creature when it enters the battlefield. These counters can be removed on a non-token creature’s death to return it to the battlefield if the number removed is equivalent to its mana cost. The creature must have a mana value of 1 or greater else the counters and effect cannot be used.
Reprieve counter.use: Return non-token creature of x mana cost on its death to the battlefield where x is the number of counters removed

Rev counter.intro: Rev counters are a type of counter introduced in Duskmourn: House of Horror.
Rev counter.description: Rev counters first appeared in Duskmourn: House of Horror on Chainsaw. It is an artifact equipment used as a weapon. The weapon must be revved to start functioning thus they represent the weapon revving up and getting stronger. It gains a counter any time a creature dies and the equipped creature gains power for each rev counter.
Rev counter.use: Marker for an increase in power of the creature the equipment is attached to

Revival counter.intro: Revival counters are a type of counter introduced in Magic: The Gathering Foundations. They can be used to return creatures to the battlefield on their death. This represents the multiple lives the creature has.
Revival counter.description:
Revival counters first appeared on the Nine-Lives Familiar in Magic: The Gathering Foundations. They represent the old saying that cats have nine lives, and thus come back.

Revival counters function similarly to the original form of Regenerate.
Revival counter.use: Marking a return to the battlefield

Ribbon counter.intro: Ribbon counters are a type of counter introduced in The Lord of the Rings Commander Decks.
Ribbon counter.description: Ribbon counters first appeared on Prize Pig in The Lord of the Rings Commander Decks. It is a creature that gains the counters whenever the player gains life with it gaining one for each amount of life gained. They are meant to represent the best-in-show animal with the pig gaining more and more ribbons as accolades. Once it reaches three or more of the counters, the counters get removed and it gets untapped. It also has an activated ability to add mana which can then be re-triggered after being untapped.
Ribbon counter.use: Marker for life gain tracking; Resource for untapping

Ritual counter.intro: Ritual counters are a type of counter introduced in Innistrad: Midnight Hunt. They act as a tracker for the transform mechanic.
Ritual counter.description: Ritual counters first appeared on the Heirloom Mirror in Innistrad: Midnight Hunt. A ritual counter can be added to via an activated ability that requires paying 1 life, 1 colorless manga, and discarding a card. These act as a tracker for the transform mechanic which triggers on 3 or more counters to become Inherited Fiend. The sacrifice of life and card represents the ritual to summon forth the demon as the result of the transformation.

Rope counter.intro: Rope counters are a type of counter introduced in Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate. They act as a protection from a card's exile effect.
Rope counter.description: Rope counters first appeared on the Fraying Line in Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate. A rope counter is added to a creature under the player's control when it enters the battlefield. During each player's upkeep, they can pay mana to add a rope counter on a creature they control. If they do not then Fraying Line and each creature without a rope counter on it is exiled and all rope counters from all creatures. This represents the creatures with the counters are saved by being attached via the rope while those without rope fall and are destroyed when a player does not continue the line.

Rust counter.intro: Rust counters are a type of counter introduced in Visions that were used to destroy artifacts.
Rust counter.description: Rust counters first appeared on Corrosion in Visions. It was an enchantment that would place a Rust counter on an opponent's artifacts each upkeep. The artifact would be destroyed when the number of counters was greater or equal to the mana value of the artifact. Artifacts destroyed this way also could not be regenerated. This represented the artifacts being corroded by rust.
Rust counter.use: Destroy artifacts with mana value equal to or less than then number of counters

Scream counter.intro: Scream counters are a type of counter introduced in Tempest. They have acted as a suspend like effect and as a +1/+0 counter.
Scream counter.description:
Scream counters first appeared on All Hallow's Eve in Legends as an unnamed counter before it was given errata to be Scream counters. It is a sorcery that is exiled with two Scream counters on it with one being removed each upkeep. Once it has no counters on it, it activates and each player returns all creatures from the graveyard to the battlefield. In this case, the counters act similarly to the Suspend mechanic and time counters.

They appeared again in Tempest on Endless Scream with a different effect. It is an Aura that can be cast with mana which makes it enter the battlefield with that many Scream counters on it granting +1/+0 for each counter on it.

Scroll counter.intro: Scroll counters are a type of counter introduced in Planechase. It has thus far excusably been used on a Plane card for some life gain and card draw effects based on the number of counters on it.
Scroll counter.description: Scroll counters first appeared on Aretopolis in Planechase. The Aretopolis was a famed museum with the Scroll counters being markers for its abilities. It gained a Scroll counter on each upkeep and whenever the player planeswalked to it. The player would then gain life for each Scroll counter on it. It also gained a Scroll counter when the Chaos symbol is rolled while also allowing cards to be drawn for the number of the counters on it.
Scroll counter.use: Life gain and card draw effects on Plane card

Shell counter.intro: Shell counter are a type of counter introduced in Weatherlight. They act as upkeep tracking for a creature becoming more powerful after several turns.
Shell counter.description: Shell counters first appeared on Roc Hatchling in Weatherlight. It enters the battlefield with 4 shell counters on it with one being removed on each upkeep. After all shell counters are removed, the creature gains additional power/toughness and flying. This represents the creature breaking out of its shell to finish hatching.

Shield counter.intro: Shield counters were introduced in Streets of New Capenna as the signature Brokers mechanic.
Shield counter.description:
Shield counters provide two benefits. First, if a permanent with a shield counter on it would be destroyed by an effect, a shield counter is removed from the permanent instead of it being destroyed. Much like how it bypasses regenerate and indestructible, reducing its toughness to 0 or less will bypass the shield counter.

The second benefit works against damage. If a permanent with a shield counter on it would be dealt damage, that damage is prevented, and a shield counter is removed from the permanent.

This prevention effect works to stop any form of damage—combat damage, damage dealt by spells like Strangle, or damage dealt because of activated or triggered abilities. However, this means that damage of any sort will remove the shield regardless of its creature's toughness, which means 1-damage effects are efficient ways of removing them. If damage can't be prevented, the shield counter is still removed, and damage is still done.

Silver counter.intro: Silver counters are a type of counter introduced in Dominaria. They are associated with the silver golem Karn and mark an exiled card that can be returned to the player's hand.
Silver counter.description: Silver counters first appeared on Karn, Scion of Urza in Dominaria. He has a loyalty ability to reveal the top two cards of a library while allowing the opponent to select one to be placed into the player's hand while the other is exiled with a Silver counter on it. Another loyalty ability can then take an exiled card with one of the counters on it and return it to the player's hand.
Silver counter.use: Marker on the exiled card for potential return to hand

Shred counter.intro: Shred counters are a type of counter introduced in Torment. They have acted as upkeep tracking an increasing number of cards to mill each turn.
Shred counter.description: Shred counters first appeared on Cephalid Vandal in Torment. It was a creature that would gain a Shred counter on each upkeep and also mill a number of cards equal to the number of Shred counters. This represented the creature shredding the player's cards from their library to the graveyard.
Shred counter.use: Upkeep tracking for number of cards to mill

Sleep counter.intro: Sleep counters are a type of counter introduced in Legends. They act as a freeze effect on creatures.
Sleep counter.description: Sleep counters first appeared on Venarian Gold in Legends as an unnamed type counter which were given errata to be Sleep counters. It is an Aura Enchantment that is placed on a creature that taps it and adds Sleep counters to it based on the additional mana cost paid for casting the enchantment. For as long as the sleep counter is on the creature it does not untap. One of the counters is removed on the controller's upkeep step. This represents the creature being put to sleep until the counters are removed at which point it wakes.

Sleight counter.intro: Sleight counters are a type of counter introduced in Ice Age. It acts as a tracker for the increased mana cost of an ability.
Sleight counter.description: Sleight counters first appeared on Chromatic Armor in Ice Age. They originally appeared as unnamed counters on the card, later errated into Sleight counters. It was an enchantment that granted protection against the color of the player's choice. It then could change that color for a mana cost equal to the number of sleight counters on it. It starts at 1 and gains another each time the ability is used making it an ever-increasing mana cost.
Sleight counter.use: Tracker for the increased mana cost of an ability

Slime counter.intro: Slime counters are a type of counter introduced in Innistrad. They have thus far been associated with the plane of Innistrad sets and have had various effects.
Slime counter.description:
Slime counters first appeared on Gutter Grime in Innistrad. It is an enchantment that gets a Slime counter placed on it whenever a nontoken creature the player controls dies, alongside creating an Ooze creature token with a power and toughness equal to the number of counters on it.

The counters appeared once again on Sludge Monster in Innistrad: Midnight Hunt. It is a creature that adds one of the counters to another creature when it enters the battlefield and when it attacks. The counters make them lose all abilities and have base power and toughness 2/2 if they are not a Horror. In its sister set Innistrad: Crimson Vow they appeared on Toxrill, the Corrosive, a Slug Horror that puts a Slime counter on all opposing creatures each end step. It acts as a −1/−1 counter on the creatures when they are not under the player's control and then whenever opposing creatures die with a Slime counter on them, Toxrill's controller creates a 1/1 black Slug creature token.

Slumber counter.intro: Slumber counters are a type of counter introduced in Commander 2018. They represent a large creature being considered a land until they are removed.
Slumber counter.description: Slumber counters first appeared on the Arixmethes, Slumbering Isle in Commander 2018. It is a legendary kraken that enters the battlefield tapped with 5 slumber counters on it. As long as it has slumber counters on it, it is considered a land rather than a creature. One of the counters is removed each time the player casts a spell. The counters represent the creature sleeping and waking up as they are removed.
Slumber counter.use: Creature is a land until counters are removed

Soot counter.intro: Soot counters are a type of counter introduced in Urza's Saga. They force players to sacrifice permanents.
Soot counter.description: Soot counters first appeared on Smokestack in Urza's Saga. It is an artifact that gets one of the Soot counters each upkeep. Then each player must sacrifice a permanent on their upkeep for every Soot counter on it. This represents the Smokestack producing pollution that destroys permanents.
Soot counter.use: Each player sacrifices a permanent on their upkeep

Soul counter.intro: Soul counters are a type of counter introduced in Commander 2020. They have often been related to sacrificial abilities involving losing life or the death of a creature.
Soul counter.description:
Soul counters first appeared on the Netherborn Altar in Commander 2020. It is an artifact with an activated ability to place a soul counter onto it alongside putting the player's commander into their hand from the command zone. As an additional cost, the player loses 3 life for each soul counter on the artifact. This represents sacrificing life to the altar. They appeared shortly thereafter in Core Set 2021 on Malefic Scythe was an equipment artifact that enters the battlefield with a soul counter on it and gains another any time its equipped creature dies. The equipped creature gains +1/+1 for each soul counter on it. This represents the scythe absorbing the soul of those that wield it.

In Innistrad: Midnight Hunt, soul counters appeared on the land Hostile Hostel which could sacrifice a creature to add a soul counter to it. These were used for the transform mechanic in that it would transform into Creeping Inn once 3 or more of the counters were on it. Following that they appeared in Streets of New Capenna on Obscura Ascendancy which is an enchantment that gains a counter if a spell is cast with a mana cost of 1+ the number of counters on it. Alongside the counter addition, it also creates a 2/2 Spirit creature token. If 5 or more counters are added, then all spirits get powered up with +3/+3.

Spark counter.intro: Several mechanics are unique to playtest cards from Mystery Booster, Mystery Booster 2, and Unknown Events. This list includes all such mechanics alphabetically from R–Z. Many of them appear on only one card.

Spite counter.intro: Spite counters are a type of counter introduced in Commander 2016. It is a multiplayer format counter used to gain an advantage from a player's defeat.
Spite counter.description: Spite counters first appeared on Curse of Vengeance in Commander 2016. It was an curse aura enchantment that enchanted the player and which would gain a Spite counter whenever that player cast a spell. Whenever the enchanted player loses the game, the player who cast the curse gains life and a card draws equal to the number of Spite counters.
Spite counter.use: Gain life and card draw on player's defeat

Spooky counter.intro: Spooky counters are a type of counter introduced on a playtest card at the 2025 Chicago Planechase Unknown event.
Spooky counter.description: Spooky counters first appeared on the Sorin's Remastered Manor plane playtest card as part of the Planechase Unknown event. The plane makes it so whenever the player planeswalks to it and during the active player's upkeep, the player adds a spooky counter on to a creature they controls, which provides a small buff. As well, whenever chaos ensues, target spooky creature "bites" (biting plus life gain) an opponent or a creature they control.

Spore counter.intro: Spore counters are counters that form the basis of the Thallid mechanic, which are a fungus tribal subtype from Fallen Empires (with some guest Elves), and are usually created during the upkeep step.
Spore counter.description:
Originally all spore counters had a secondary ability with a cost of "Remove three spore counters from this card:", but with several different effects; the most common of these was to create a 1/1 Saproling token. Its return in Time Spiral expanded on this using Thallid Devourer as a basis; there would be an upkeep spore counter ability, a Saproling-creating ability, and sometimes a Saproling-sacrificing ability. Alchemy: Ixalan combined these two aspects into Propagator Primordium.

This allows the player to have a spore counter and a Saproling token-based economy.

Stash counter.intro: Stash counters are a type of counter introduced in Streets of New Capenna.
Stash counter.description:
Stash counters are used to track a player's use of resources and are then used to convert that stash into another resource.

Stash counters first appeared on the Glittering Stockpile in Streets of New Capenna. It is a treasure artifact with an activated ability to give along with adding a stash counter to it. It has a second ability to sacrifice the treasure to gain mana of any color equal to the number of counters on it. This represents stashing the mana for later.

Bloomburrow saw a return of stash counters on Hoarder's Overflow, which function similarly to Glittering Stockpile.

Magic: The Gathering Foundations combined stash counters with Tinybones habit of stealing things to allow players to steal their opponents cards as they discard them.

Storage counter.intro: Storage counters are used by storage lands to store surplus mana for use in later turns.

Story counter.intro: Story counters are a type of counter introduced in the Phyrexia: All Will Be One commander decks.
Story counter.description: Story counters first appeared on the Staff of the Storyteller in the Phyrexia: All Will Be One commander decks. It is an artifact that gains a story counter anytime one or more creature Tokens are created. The artifact also creates a Spirit token when it first enters the battlefield so it starts with one counter on it. It then has an activated ability to pay and remove a story counter to draw a card.

Strife counter.intro: Strife counters are a type of counter introduced in Commander 2011. They acted as an upkeep tracker for an increasing power bonus on all creatures each turn.
Strife counter.description: Strife counters first appeared on Crescendo of War in Commander 2011. It would gain a Strife counter on each upkeep and then would grant all attacking and blocking creatures +1/+0 for each Strife counter on the enchantment. This represented the creatures gaining an advantage and being empowered the longer the conflict lasted.
Strife counter.use: Upkeep tracking for increasing power gain

Study counter.intro: Study counters are a type of counter introduced in Stronghold. They have been used in various sets for various unrelated effects.
Study counter.description:
Study counters first appeared on Pursuit of Knowledge in Stronghold. It was an enchantment that allowed for the skipping of a draw to add a Study counter. Once three Study counters were accumulated, they could then be sacrificed in exchange for seven cards to be drawn.

Innistrad saw the return of Study counters on Grimoire of the Dead which allowed for a counter to be placed in exchange for discarding a card. At three Study counters, it could then be sacrificed, which moves all creatures from all graveyards onto the battlefield under the player's control as a Black Zombie on top of existing colors and types.

Kianne, Dean of Substance was the first creature to use Study counters. One could be placed on non-land cards exiled by her first ability. It then had another ability to create Fractal tokens with +1/+1 counters equal to the number of mana values among the exiled cards with study counters. Imbraham, Dean of Theory exiles X cards off the library with Study counters on them and puts one into hand; the two synergize with Imbraham putting study counters en masse, including lands, which guarantees another value for Kianne's Fractal ability. Conversely, Kianne's exile ability gives a faster and cheaper selection for Imbraham's card ability.

Alchemy Horizons: Baldur's Gate had Vhal, Eager Scholar which is a digital-only card that uses Study counters for effects of the Specialize mechanic. After specializing, the counters were removed and a scaling effect occurred based on how many were on it.

Stun counter.intro: Stun counters are counters that prevent tapped permanents from untapping. They were introduced in Dominaria United. Stun counters are an evolution of the freeze mechanic and are currently considered evergreen.
Stun counter.description:
Stun counters act similar to a Freeze mechanic. They keep permanents out of the action for an extended period. Freeze effects restrain themselves to prevent the next untap during the untap step, but using stun counters lets the freeze persist beyond the first turn of effect. This is most pertinent for instants and sorceries as opposed to Auras. Additionally, multiple stun counters could be put on a target. This gave another development tweak for tempo tap spells, as "draw a card" as a rider (such as Crippling Chill) meant all blue decks would have a reason to take it, but a spell like Freeze in Place would usually be a liability for decks aiming to win through card advantage.

The use of counters makes for better memory tracking, if the source that "froze" is no longer apparent. It also allows for compounding, whereas multiple freeze effects will overlap on itself.

Stun counters are considered to be evergreen. Applying stun counters to other permanents is considered primarily in blue and secondary in white. They are not expected to be used by other colors. By the beginning of 2025, Mark Rosewater had noted that on the Storm Scale stun counters fall somewhere between evergreen and deciduous.

Supply counter.intro: Supply counters are a type of counter introduced in Bloomburrow.
Supply counter.description: Supply counters were introduced in Bloomburrow on Stocking the Pantry. They represent the increasing number of nuts stored by the squirrelfolk of Bloomburrow. They allow players to convert buffing their creatures into future cards. The enchantment gains one of the counters anytime the player adds a +1/+1 counter to a creature. It then has an activated ability to payer 2 colorless mana to remove one of the counters and draw a card.
Supply counter.use: Marker for +1/+1 counters; Resource for drawing a card

Suspect counter.intro: Suspect counters are a type of counter introduced in Innistrad: Crimson Vow. They are used as an additional resource to draw a card.
Suspect counter.description: Suspect counters first appeared on the Investigator's Journal in Innistrad: Crimson Vow. It is a clue artifact that enters the battlefield with counters on it with their number equal to the highest number of creatures a player controls. It then has an activated ability that uses the counters as an additional resource to draw a card. The counters represent the creatures being suspects and the cards being noted to assist in stopping them.

Takeover counter.intro: Takeover counters are a type of counter introduced in Doctor Who. They are used to track cards in exile for related effects.
Takeover counter.description: Takeover counters first appeared on The Master, Formed Anew in Doctor Who. They act as markers on the card exiled with it to allow it to become a copy of that creature. This allows for future copies of The Master, Formed Anew to become a copy of cards exiled by previous versions.

Task counter.intro: Task counters are a type of counter introduced in Theros Beyond Death. They mark the number of turns a creature cannot be used.
Task counter.description: Task counters first appeared on the Heliod's Punishment in Theros Beyond Death. It is an aura enchantment that enters the battlefield with 4 Task counters on it. The enchanted creature loses all its abilities and cannot attack or block until all the Task counters are removed. It has an activated ability to remove one of the counters. Once all are removed, the enchantment is destroyed. The counters represent tasks the creature must complete before it can do anything else.
Task counter.use: Creature can’t attack or block and loses all abilities.

Theft counter.intro: Theft counters are a type of counter introduced in Champions of Kamigawa. They are built upon damage to the enemy player and could be used for a tutor's ability.
Theft counter.description: Theft counters first appeared on Night Dealings in Champions of Kamigawa. It would gain Theft counters for any amount of damage dealt by any source controlled by the player to the opponent. It then could remove Theft counters and tutor for a card with a mana value equivalent to the number of Theft counters being removed. Their creation from damaging the opponent player and getting a card from the library using them represent theft from the enemy to gain an advantage.
Theft counter.use: Tutor for a card with mana value equal to the number of counters

Ticket counter.intro: Ticket counters are a type of resource counter that may be placed on a player. They were introduced in Unfinity.
Ticket counter.description:
Most cards that let you sticker give you tickets. Players are not forced to spend them, but you can’t play any ability or power/toughness stickers without them. The cheapest ticket cost for stickers is 2. Some cards tell you to use a specific sticker while others are general.

A ticket marker will become available to keep track of your tickets. The plain text symbol for tickets is {TK}.

Tide counter.intro: Tide counters are a type of counter introduced in Fallen Empires. The counters accumulate, with a negative ability for only having one, a positive ability for having three counters and resetting at four or more.
Tide counter.description: Tide counters first appeared on Homarid and Tidal Influence in Fallen Empires. Both operate similarly; both permanents start with one counter and gain another every upkeep, and whenever four counters are on them they are all removed, giving them a four-turn cycle that evokes the movement of the tides. At exactly one counter — "low tide" — there is a negative effect: Homarid gets −1/−1 and Tidal Influence gives all blue creatures −2/−0. At exactly three counters — "high tide" — there is a positive effect: Homarid gets +1/+1 and Tidal Influence gives blue creatures +2/+0.

Time counter.intro: Time counters are counters that are usually removed during the upkeep step. If the last time counter on a card is removed, an effect will occur. They are especially associated with Time Spiral block and the Vanishing and Suspend abilities.

Tower counter.intro: Tower counters are a type of counter introduced in Eventide. They act as a resource for an alternate win condition.
Tower counter.description: Tower counters first appeared on Helix Pinnacle in Eventide. It has an ability which can create Tower counters in exchange for mana on each turn. If at the beginning of the player's upkeep, they have 100 or more Tower counters on it, then they win the game. This represents the counters stacking towards the pinnacle of victory.

Training counter.intro: Training counters are a type of counter introduced in Champions of Kamigawa. They turn creatures into Samurai with bushido.
Training counter.description: Training counters first appeared on Sensei Golden-Tail in Champions of Kamigawa. It is a creature with an activated ability to place a Training counter on a creature. The creature gains bushido 1 and becomes a Samurai in addition to its other creature types. This represents the creature being trained to become a Samurai.
Training counter.use: Creature gains bushido 1 and becomes a Samurai

Trap counter.intro: Trap counters are a type of counter introduced in Scourge. They are placed on lands that give them a sacrificial ability to deal damage to creatures.
Trap counter.description: Trap counters first appeared on Trap Digger in Scourge. It is a creature with an activated ability to place Trap counters on lands under the Player's control. These lands can then be sacrificed to deal 3 damage to a creature without flying. This represents the land being trapped and activating on the creature with flying creatures being immune as they can stay above the land.
Trap counter.use: Sacrifice land to deal damage to non-flying creature

Treasure counter.intro: Treasure counters are a type of counter introduced in Onslaught. It was used as an upkeep tracker for later use to steal a creature.
Treasure counter.description: Treasure counters first appeared on Legacy's Allure in Tempest. A counter was added to the enchantment during each upkeep. The enchantment could then be sacrificed to gain control of a creature with a power less than the number of treasure counters.
Treasure counter.use: Upkeep tracking for Stealing a creature

Unity counter.intro: Unity counters are a type of counter introduced in Aether Revolt. They are created via the Revolt mechanic and grant +1/+1 to all creatures that are under the player's control.
Unity counter.description: Unity counters first appeared on Call for Unity in Aether Revolt. They are created on the Enchantment via the Revolt mechanic. A unity counter is added at the beginning of the end step if a permanent that the player controlled left the battlefield during the turn. They then give +1/+1 for each Unity counter to all creatures under the player's control.

Unlock counter.intro: Unlock counters are a type of counter introduced in Murders at Karlov Manor.
Unlock counter.description: Unlock counters are used as a thematic representation of solving a cryptex. As players gather clues (collect evidence) to the code, they gain more unlock counters on their Cryptex. Five or more unlock counters grant access to the cryptex's contents.

Valor counter.intro: Valor counters are a type of counter introduced in Innistrad: Midnight Hunt. They give all creatures under the player's control +1/+1.
Valor counter.description: Valor counters first appeared on the Intrepid Adversary in Innistrad: Midnight Hunt. The card is the white constituent of the Adversary cycle, each of which has a functional "multikicker" cost that gives +1/+1 counters to the creature and another effect for each payment. White's effect was chosen to be a continuous team pump for each payment, but this had tracking issues if it was based on the +1/+1 counters, as they are easily manipulated. Thus, the effect was changed to use Valor counters and the team pump effect was changed from "other creatures you control..." to "creatures you control...".

Velocity counter.intro: Velocity counters are a type of counter introduced in Alliances. They act as a marker representing a form of thematic increasing speed.
Velocity counter.description:
Velocity counters first appeared on Tornado in Alliances. It is an enchantment with the ability to destroy any permanent while adding a Velocity counter to itself. The player must then pay 3 life for each counter on it when activating the ability again. This forces an increasing cost to use the ability to represent the increasing speed of the tornado.

The counters appeared again on Daredevil Dragster in Aether Revolt. One of the counters is added to it whenever it attacks or blocks. Whenever it gains 2 of these counters it must be sacrificed with the player drawing two cards. In this case, they represent the increasing speed and destruction of the vehicle.
Velocity counter.use: Marker for a form of thematic increasing speed

Verse counter.intro: Verse counters are used by a set of enchantments from Urza's Saga and their successor in Modern Horizons, as well as one creature from Magic 2015.
Verse counter.description:
The enchantments that use Verse counters are part of two cycles (one at uncommon and one at rare):

Uncommon cycle: Serra's Hymn, Lilting Refrain, Vile Requiem, Torch Song, and War Dance Rare cycle: Serra's Liturgy, Recantation, Discordant Dirge, Rumbling Crescendo, and Midsummer Revel

If a player controls one of these growing enchantments during their upkeep, they may put a verse counter on it. The enchantment can be sacrificed for an effect multiplied by the number of verse counters on it at the time of sacrificing.

Yisan, the Wanderer Bard was printed, which, although it functions differently than the enchantments, uses verse counters to reflect the musical theme of the card.

Aria of Flame from Modern Horizons functions in the direct tradition of the earlier enchantments.

Vitality counter.intro: Vitality counters are a type of counter introduced in Alpha that represents previously taken damage that can be converted back into life.
Vitality counter.description: Vitality counters first appeared on Living Artifact in Alpha and reprinted in various core sets up through Fifth Edition. They were originally introduced as an unnamed counter type which was later given errata to be Vitality counters. Living Artifact was an enchantment that would gain a Vitality counter for every piece of damage dealt to the player. Then during upkeep, an ability could be activated to gain +1 for each Vitality counter removed.
Vitality counter.use: Convert previously taken damage into life

Void counter.intro: Void counters are a type of counter introduced in Modern Horizons 2. They have been used for various exile-related effects.
Void counter.description:
Void counters first appeared on the Dauthi Voidwalker in Modern Horizons 2. It is a creature that makes it so an opponent's cards are exiled with a void counter instead of going to the graveyard. It then has a sacrificial activated ability to play one of the opponent's exiled cards with a void counter without paying its mana cost. The counters represent the exiled cards being in the void with the voidwalker having the ability to cast one.

They appeared once again in Dungeons & Dragons: Adventures in the Forgotten Realms on Sphere of Annihilation. The player can cast it with additional mana so it will enter the battlefield with that many Void counters on it.
