Upon the player's next upkeep, all creatures and planeswalkers on the battlefield and in graveyards with mana cost less than the number of counters are exiled. This represents the cards being annihilated into the void.

Volatile counter.intro: Volatile counter was a counter with an innate ability: "Whenever a permanent with a volatile counter on it went to the graveyard from the battlefield, the volatile counter does 2 damage to target opponent". It was created by Mark Gottlieb for Aether Revolt, but later in the design process, it was put out due to complexity and flavor issues.

Vortex counter.intro: Vortex counters are a type of counter introduced in Alliances.
Vortex counter.description: Vortex counters first appeared on Energy Vortex in Mirage. It is an enchantment with an ability to add vortex counters on it for mana. At the beginning of a chosen opponent's upkeep, they take 3 damage for each Vortex counter until they pay for each. All of the counters are then removed from the enchantment on the player's next upkeep forcing them to pay to add more.

Vow counter.intro: Vow counters are a type of counter introduced in Commander 2021. They have no inherent rules meaning.
Vow counter.description: Vow counters first appeared on the Promise of Loyalty in Commander 2021. It is a sorcery that lets each player place a vow counter on a creature they control while sacrificing all their others. Creatures with the counter cannot attack the player or planeswalkers they control for as long as they have the vow counter on them. This represents the creatures taking a vow of friendship.
Vow counter.use: Creatures cannot attack players who cast sorcery that created them

Voyage counter.intro: Voyage counters are a type of counter introduced in Kaldheim. They are related to Cosima, the Kaldheim God of the Voyage.
Voyage counter.description: Voyage counters first appeared on the Cosima, God of the Voyage in Kaldheim. The player can choose to exile Cosima on their upkeep which does so with a voyage counter on it. While exiled, it may also gain more voyage counters for each land that enters the battlefield under the player's control. In place of any of these additions, the player can instead choose to return it to the battlefield at which point it gains +1/+1 counters equal to the number of counters on it and the player can draw that many cards as well. The counters represent Cosima voyaging to different lands and gaining power and knowledge from them.
Voyage counter.use: Creates +1/+1 counter along with drawing a card

Wage counter.intro: Wage counters are a type of counter introduced in Alliances. They were used as an upkeep tracker to represent an increasing mana payment required to keep a creature under the Player's control.
Wage counter.description: Wage counters first appeared on Rogue Skycaptain in Alliances. It was a creature that would get a Wage counter for each upkeep as a Mercenary. Then the player would be required to pay 2 mana for each Wage counter on the creature or else it would transfer to the opponent player's control. This represented the mercenary going rogue and switching sides due to not being paid.
Wage counter.use: Upkeep tracking for mana payment required to keep creature under control

Winch counter.intro: Winch counters are a type of counter introduced in Mercadian Masques. They act as a resource for moving creatures from the player's hand onto the battlefield.
Winch counter.description: Winch counters first appeared on Mercadian Lift in Mercadian Masques. It is an artifact with the ability to add Winch counters to itself. It can then use another ability to remove counters and place a creature with that mana value from the player's hand onto the battlefield without paying its mana cost. This represents the Winch of the Lift moving the creatures between the two zones.
Winch counter.use: Resource to move creatures from hand to battlefield

Wind counter.intro: Wind counters are a type of counter introduced in Arabian Nights. They are used for effects on cards with a wind theme.
Wind counter.description:
Wind counters first appeared on Cyclone in Arabian Nights where they were originally known as "chips" before being given errata to be Wind counters. It is an enchantment that gets a Wind counter for each upkeep and forces the player to pay per counter on it or else it will be sacrificed. If the player pays, then the Cyclone deals damage equal to the number of Wind counters to the opponent player.

The counters appeared once again on Freyalise's Winds in Ice Age. It was an enchantment that would add a Wind counter to any permanent that became tapped. It acts as a replacement for untapping with all the counters being removed instead of untapping the permanent.

Wish counter.intro: Wish counters are a type of counter introduced in Magic 2010. They have been used on various cards as a resource for activated abilities that have a type of Tutor effect for getting a card from the library. Thus far, all of its uses start with 3 wish counters to represent the popular mythology concept of "3 wishes" with each use of an ability representing a wish for a card.
Wish counter.description:
Wish counters first appeared on Djinn of Wishes in Magic 2010. They act as a resource for the creature's ability in that it starts with 3 of the counters and then can spend them in an activated ability to reveal and play the top card of the library without its cost or exile it.

Ring of Three Wishes in Magic 2014 saw the counters return. It also entered play with 3 wish counters which could be spent on its ability to search the library for a specific card and put it into the player's hand.

The counters returned in Throne of Eldraine on Wishclaw Talisman which similarly enters the battlefield with 3 wish counters. They allow a player to similarly search the library for a specific card but the Talisman changes control to an opponent player after each use.

Wreck counter.intro: Wreck counters are a type of counter introduced in Alchemy: Aetherdrift.
Wreck counter.description: Wreck counters first appeared on the Spectacle of Destruction. One is added to the enhancement whenever one or more creatures dies. At the beginning of the player's upkeep, one of the counters is removed and they seek a nonland card. The counters represent the dangers of racing in the Ghirapur Grand Prix and the attention fans bring as a result.
